note: Step 4. How each scenario changes walking before a fall. Numbers come from the sources below; the mapping from a between-group difference (fallers vs non-fallers) to a within-episode change in the seconds before a fall is OUR ASSUMPTION and must be stated as such.

HAUSDORFF2001.citation: Hausdorff JM, Rios DA, Edelberg HK. Gait variability and fall risk in community-living older adults: a 1-year prospective study. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2001;82(8):1050-6.
HAUSDORFF2001.finding: stride time variability 106 ± 30 ms in later fallers (n=20) vs 49 ± 4 ms in non-fallers (n=32); only variability separated fallers

HAUSDORFF1997.citation: Hausdorff JM, Edelberg HK, Mitchell SL, Goldberger AL, Wei JY. Increased gait unsteadiness in community-dwelling elderly fallers. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 1997;78(3):278-83.
HAUSDORFF1997.finding: all stride-to-stride variability measures greater in fallers (p<.0002); walking speed similar to non-fallers

VERGHESE2009.citation: Verghese J, Holtzer R, Lipton RB, Wang C. Quantitative gait markers and incident fall risk in older adults. J Gerontol A. 2009;64(8):896-901.
VERGHESE2009.finding: fall risk ratio 1.069 per 10 cm/s slower gait; stride length variability RR 1.076, swing time variability RR 1.007

ROBINOVITCH2013.citation: Robinovitch SN et al. Video capture of the circumstances of falls in elderly people residing in long-term care. Lancet. 2013;381:47-54.
ROBINOVITCH2013.finding: 227 falls: incorrect weight shifting 41%, trip/stumble 21%, hit/bump 11%, loss of support 11%, collapse 11%, slip 3%; forward walking 24%, standing 13%, sitting down 12%

MOL2019.citation: Mol A et al. Orthostatic hypotension and falls in older adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis. J Am Med Dir Assoc. 2019.

FOG_PD_REVIEW.citation: Review citing Pelicioni et al.: 61% of 2,043 prospectively recorded falls in people with Parkinson's disease were freezing-related (secondhand; original not checked).

OUR_RADAR.citation: normal_gait_stats.json (lee/kim walking, 11-05/11-12) and fall_moment_stats.json (10-12/10-13 staged falls)

freeze_collapse.basis: short shuffling steps then a halt; slower gait raises risk (VERGHESE2009)

dizzy_collapse.basis: standing still with growing body sway; no walking

trip_fall.basis: normal walking until the trip: kept as a check that the model is not credited for unpredictable falls

negatives.sit_chair: walk, stop, sit: centre drops to 0.85-0.95 m in 0.8-1.5 s (10-13 chair: z p10 0.90)
negatives.crouch: walk, stop, crouch 1-4 s: centre drops near floor then rises (10-13 crouch: z p10 −0.1)
